focuses.name: The Ending Stages of Clintonomics
focuses.description: The ending months of the administration are upon us and as such we should start gearing up for the next election.

focuses.name: Enjoying a Continued Surplus
focuses.description: The budget is in the green and now we can watch as the money rolls in.

focuses.name: The Rise of the Internet
focuses.description: The dawn of a new age is upon us, as such we must embrace the newest forms of technology and stay ahead of the game.

focuses.name: Limited Industrial Expansion
focuses.description: The administration isn't over quite yet, as such we must leave a mark and target economic growth in the Blue Collar heartland that is the Rust Belt.

focuses.name: Late Renewable Investments
focuses.description: The scares of the past with the depleting rate of fossil fuels is a good cause for concern, lest we be too reliant on one such form of energy, we are certainly doomed to adapt to the changing world when the time comes.

focuses.name: Gearing up for the 43 Administration
focuses.description: The time has come for me to leave office, but the party can still win, as such we must direct these last weeks to the hopeful securing of another term with our party at the helm.

focuses.name: 2000 Democrat Victory
focuses.description: Through determination we have won over our Republican adversaries.

focuses.name: Early Green Energy Investments
focuses.description: We must look to our nation's future, renewable energy is on the rise and we must make sure this momentum is kept.

focuses.name: Increased Healthcare Spending
focuses.description: With rebudgeting towards healthcare, we can help retain and grow our population, we hopefully can keep this through a Republican Administration, let alone in the general future as a whole though.

focuses.name: New Millennia Tax Reforms
focuses.description: The newest tax reforms we plan shall increase our economic growth by repurposing it towards automation and construction efforts to grow the economy.

focuses.name: Targeted Regulations
focuses.description: Through targeting more urbanized states we can expand the economic sectors there which should boost our economy as a whole.

focuses.name: Social Security Improvements
focuses.description: With re-budgeting towards Social Security, we can help retain and grow our population and expand domestic markets/ consumption, we hopefully can keep this through a Republican Administration, let alone in the general future as a whole though.

focuses.name: The Green Regulatory Commission
focuses.description: The establishment of a green regulation commission will allow the prioritization of the environmental impact of future construction projects, but it may cost us construction efficiency, nevertheless we need to start looking after the planet and our peoples health as well.

focuses.name: Neighborly Trade Agreements
focuses.description: Through negotiations and what we believe are fair trade agreements, we shall expand our trade influence over our neighbors in the hopes of securing the North American markets.

focuses.name: Pushing the Anti-Smoking Initiative
focuses.description: The citizens need healthier lives and as such we must push campaigns to show the negative effects of the tobacco industry as a whole.

focuses.name: Dealing with Anti-Globalization Protest
focuses.description: Agitators have come to protest our recent changes towards better integrating and cooperating with foreign economies, as such we must deal with these ignorant individuals in a discreet manner when in the eyes of the public.

focuses.name: State Visit to Vietnam
focuses.description: The history of our relations with Vietnam is shaky, but it's better to be late to remedy this than to sit and let a passive build of tension arise. As such we must conduct a state visit to Vietnam.

focuses.name: Helping Al Gore in the Coming Election
focuses.description: The president's term is almost up and Al Gore, his VP, is looking to be the best replacement for the next term. We must ensure that he is well liked in the public eye so he will be elected.

focuses.name: 2000 Republican Victory
focuses.description: Through determination we have won over our Democrat adversaries.

focuses.name: Early Administration Deregulation
focuses.description: The previous administration hindered economic growth, by cutting some red tape certain states can expand their economies faster.

focuses.name: Increased Military Spending
focuses.description: The world is an ever changing place, as such we must keep on top of our military viability if we are to remain the global superpower.

focuses.name: The 2001 Tax cuts
focuses.description: The people know what they need, as such these tax cuts should help them to pursue their needs.

focuses.name: Education Reforms
focuses.description: Children are the nation's future; as such we must begin to reform the school systems with the latest technologies.

focuses.name: Limited Deregulation Efforts
focuses.description: Key government legislation has slowed down the economic growth as a whole, we should cut these to allow for faster development and output of goods and services.

focuses.name: Reform the Financial Sector
focuses.description: The financial sector is the biggest GDP grower, as such we should reform it to allow for its continual and lest we say, exceptional growth in the sector itself.

focuses.name: Central America Free Trade Agreement
focuses.description: The Monroe Doctrine must be enforced even to this day, but we must seek friendlier ties to the nations near and around the Panama canal if we are to secure political and economic dominance in the Americas markets.

focuses.name: 2004 Democrat Victory
focuses.description: Through determination we have won over our Republican adversaries.

focuses.name: The Light Green Deal
focuses.description: The Light Green Deal is desperately needed before we do any more damage to the environment than already dealt.

focuses.name: Education Investments
focuses.description: To invest in education is to invest in the future of our children, as such we must make sure we help make the future for generations to come.

focuses.name: Economic Crack Downs
focuses.description: The corporations are exploiting the people, as such we must enact severe regulatory policies to preemptively prevent the further expansion of such businesses.

focuses.name: Social Security Expansion
focuses.description: Our people must have the benefits of a retirement. But the current state of the Social Security Program is a mess. Through restructuring and reallocating existing budgets and resources we can make the program more efficient and less costly on the average tax payer.

focuses.name: Federal Economic Funding Initiative
focuses.description: We must rival the world in GDP growth, as such we must invest in the modern money makers which are the office structures and the financial markets.

focuses.name: Public Works
focuses.description: Through public work projects we can help build the interconnected nature to incentivize local consumption and economic growth.

focuses.name: 2007 Tax Reform
focuses.description: These new taxes should help to cover new government initiatives, after all, it is the government's job to help its people.

focuses.name: 2004 Republican Victory
focuses.description: To another term won against our Democrat adversaries.

focuses.name: Military Contracts
focuses.description: To keep our military stocked up we must seek the growth of military contracts to keep up with demands.

focuses.name: Economic Deregulation
focuses.description: To continue expansion we must deregulate the economy further. We can do this by attacking "core" legislation that is full of barriers to business growth and new start-ups.

focuses.name: Business Investments
focuses.description: Limited government investments into key businesses will propel our nation's GDP and create more jobs as a result of the "stimulation" towards the targeted economic sectors.

focuses.name: Healthcare Reforms
focuses.description: The Healthcare system is too heavily burdened by regulations which cripples initiative and research, as such we must make key changes to the system as a whole.

focuses.name: Less Red Tape
focuses.description: Targeted states through their own regulatory commissions will allow the expansion of their economies by self assessing their needs and available space to build new businesses and so on.

focuses.name: Budget Balancing
focuses.description: We need to find ways to balance our budget and minimize the deficit so that our economy can run smoothly.

focuses.name: 2007 Tax Cuts
focuses.description: Cutting taxes is good stimulation for the economy, provides self made incentives to buy products, save for personal ventures and allows businesses to use the extra capital to expand and create more jobs.

focuses.name: National Urbanization I
focuses.description: The generations change and the economy grows, looks as if the nation on the whole is expanding as well.

focuses.name: 2008 Democrat Victory
focuses.description: To the victors we are, another potential term secured against the opposition.

focuses.name: 2009 Tax Reforms
focuses.description: Through new taxes we can incentivize GDP growth where we know it counts.

focuses.name: Expanding Environmental Safeguards
focuses.description: The environment is paramount and states with more environment around them must have stricter guidelines.

focuses.name: Focused Inter-Economic Deals
focuses.description: China is home to the best ways in which to get cheap goods, as such we must open up and embrace our compatriots from across the Pacific.

focuses.name: Social Security Improvements
focuses.description: Through further restructuring and better streamlining of processing data and needs, our taxpayers will be paying less into Social Security while keeping if not expanding the benefits they get when they retire. This will boost confidence and morale which can make people more productive in the workplace.

focuses.name: Healthcare Improvements
focuses.description: We must look to our British counterparts and see that medicare for all can be for all, as such we must still compromise with the opposition if we are to pass such a "dangerous" policy.

focuses.name: Decreased Policing
focuses.description: Crime is on the decline in some areas and up in others, therefore we must "limit" policing efforts and "redirect" it to other means if needed.

focuses.name: Urbanization Efforts
focuses.description: Urbanization is the most efficient way to have people and an economy function without long times between different stages in the manufacturing process. As such we must consolidate and grow our economic hubs.

focuses.name: 2008 Republican Victory
focuses.description: We've secured another victory for our party, let's make the most of it.

focuses.name: Rural Redevelopments
focuses.description: We must focus on the core of our nation, blue collar individuals and the vast rural areas of the nation, to do so we must invest into state economies which fit such parameters.

focuses.name: Overseas Trade Deals
focuses.description: We must keep up our global fiscal footprint, as such, we must create an atmosphere of cooperation between us and nations deemed important to their respective continental and or regional markets.

focuses.name: Relaxing Environmental Regulations
focuses.description: We must deregulate these cumbersome "Green" regulations in order to better incentivize the future entrepreneur to want to start a new business.

focuses.name: Policing Initiatives
focuses.description: With our new police programs rolling out, we should now be able to build better community involvement and tackle certain major criminal hot spots from growing any further and quash others.

focuses.name: The Military Industrial Complex
focuses.description: The expansion and renewal of key military contracts will allow for our armed forces to be better equipped and face less logistical shortcomings.

focuses.name: Military Budgetary Increase
focuses.description: The new fiscal year will be adjusted in accordance with the rising changes in the global environment, as such we must invest more funding into our armed services if we are to keep pace.

focuses.name: 2011 Tax Cuts
focuses.description: To better incentivize domestic consumption and growth we must cut key taxes and change around and or in a reductionary manner tax codes which affect all classes of citizenry that way businesses can reinvest the extra capital into job creation, workers can buy and afford more stuff and hopefully give more people the potential opportunity to make their own business.

focuses.name: Wrapping up the 2011 Fiscal Year
focuses.description: The presidential term is coming to an end and hopefully we can secure a victory to bring more progress to our economic agenda.

focuses.name: 2012 Democrat Victory
focuses.description: To the victors we are, another potential term secured against the opposition.

focuses.name: Riding the Green Wave
focuses.description: The people want a greener tomorrow and we can use this fervor to push our plans.

focuses.name: Renewable Investments
focuses.description: We must appeal to our strongest voting bases and for that we need to show them the fruits of their voting investment.

focuses.name: Renewable Refitting
focuses.description: To combat the general increase in carbon emissions we must seek to make new building codes when new industries attempt to start up and or existing ones attempt expansion.

focuses.name: Renewable R&D Department
focuses.description: Not every mode of transport can be efficient by electric power, we must invest further into any renewable forms to allow for the widespread adoption of it among more than just the roadways.

focuses.name: Infrastructure Act of 2014
focuses.description: The Northeast Corridor is crumbling and as such we must make direct investments to keep it operational.

focuses.name: Blue Chip Investments
focuses.description: We must focus on our voting bases if we are to maintain popularity among the voters for the coming election.

focuses.name: The Digital Classroom Act
focuses.description: Not everyone can enjoy the luxury of private schools, to that I say we must modernize our public schools to the same degree. After all, the youth are our future.

focuses.name: 2012 Republican Victory
focuses.description: We've secured another victory for our party, let's make the most of it.

focuses.name: The Anti-Opium Act
focuses.description: We need to counter in a more effective way the modern Opium War which is consuming America today, with that we must increase the budget towards anti-drug units and special cartel tracking units if we are to begin any kind of effective measures.

focuses.name: Deregulating the Renewable Sector
focuses.description: The rise of environmentalism must be dealt with through our own means and as such if there is such a concern then we must cut back key regulations to allow more to invest in the market for renewable sources.

focuses.name: The Osmium Act
focuses.description: New feats in technology require increasing amounts of rare earth elements, to combat foreign dependencies we must increase our domestic production.

focuses.name: Gulf Coast Defence Act
focuses.description: With the cyber scares of recent memory and the more bold actions of some of our adversaries both known and unknown, we must seek to create an iron grip on the Gulf of Mexico, lest they attempt to send any naval forces to blockade the vital trading hub that is the Gulf coast states.

focuses.name: The Standard Classroom Act
focuses.description: The private sector has shown schools can be both equitable and educational, however there must be a form of national standardization if we are to allow a fair and straightforward curriculum. The Standard Classroom Act shall do that and reduce the federal budget towards this as well.

focuses.name: Red Chip Investments
focuses.description: With the next coming presidential term, we must solidify our support by directly investing in states which are loyal and or look to be turning purple as to keep their loyalty.

focuses.name: The Great Plains Act
focuses.description: To encourage job growth and to combat mass urbanization, we must look towards the emptier states such as the Great Plains, these states produce more than enough food for domestic and export consumption that we must invest in diversifying their economies to bring more people from the crowded cities of Atlanta, New York and so forth.

focuses.name: Urbanization II
focuses.description: The job market is on the rise...good thing cause we need it.

focuses.name: 2016 Democrat Victory
focuses.description: Through determination we have won over our Republican adversaries.

focuses.name: Blue Cross Act
focuses.description: The medical care of our citizens matter, but we must be able to incentivize the growth in jobs, so we must create building and staffing standards for all facilities to increase quality and quantity of treatments.

focuses.name: Red Shield Act
focuses.description: We must supplement our previous legislation with another, we must show the world that American healthcare is the best care.

focuses.name: The Better Tomorrow Act
focuses.description: Changing some of the regulations and better standardizing the contradicting regulations related to zoning and building will result in more developmental lands to become available, however it will take a little longer to build these new buildings to code.

focuses.name: Blue States Bailout
focuses.description: To solidify our image we must hold firm to states where they are blue and or purple, this should help in the coming election cycle.

focuses.name: 2016 Republican Victory
focuses.description: We've secured another victory for our party, let's make the most of it.

focuses.name: The Lithium Act
focuses.description: New feats in technology require increasing amounts of rare earth elements, to combat foreign dependencies we must increase our domestic production.

focuses.name: Greater Plains Act
focuses.description: Our core voting base is in the more rural states, however if we can create a nice dispersion of jobs to grow these states we can change the electoral college and the house itself via the census.

focuses.name: The Better Business Act
focuses.description: With the population growing more and more we must roll back some more redundant regulations to speed up construction efforts to create new jobs.

focuses.name: Blue Collar Programs
focuses.description: With more people losing faith in things like Obamacare and other efforts, we can appeal to average people by changing and strengthening the regulations around corporate provided plans. Some may not like this approach, but it will appeal to more than that will disapprove.

focuses.name: The 2000 Joint Military Exercises
focuses.description: The US army will conduct joint military exercises in relation to certain NATO allies.

focuses.name: The Pentagon Wars
focuses.description: Towards the end of the Cold War and into the new millennia, a brewing internal struggle began in the upper echelons of the Pentagon and the overall US Military apparatus. Old hands believed that the costs of new machines and weapons of war would be mere novelties which the enemy could use to bankrupt us. While on the other side you had the young bloods and innovators, which believed that modern radar and other innovations in military arms would define and shape the modern battlefield. This internal struggle has been sensationalized by media outlets and hollywood, but only those with clearance know the true outcome.

focuses.name: United States Army
focuses.description: Founded as the Continental Army during the American Revolutionary War, the United States Army is one of the three main pillars of the armed forces of these United States. Throughout its history the army has seen countless tones of innovation as well as its fair share of corruption. But in the modern age the branch faces a new challenge. With the peak of technological innovations on the rise the divide between tech vs tact is ever growing into destructive means. Lost money, R&D projects going over budget by metrics not seen in decades as well as just the internal sabotage of fellow officers and generals means there is much to do. The question is, where to start?

focuses.name: The Five Star Folly
focuses.description: The modern battlefield is one of both will and determination, not gizmos and gadgets. We must therefore fine tune and retool our training efforts, our structure and the adaptability of our forces with the equipment we already have. R&D will be cut and relegated to quality of life improvements, small arms enhancements, as well as logistical prowess.

focuses.name: Infantry Doctrine Debate
focuses.description: In order to be efficient as well as cut costs, we must look into the core of what makes our army function. This core pillar is that of the common soldier, the infantry. Currently there are three main doctrines which pressed on through and past the Cold Wars' conclusion. The Light Infantry Doctrine, the Mobile Infantry Doctrine and the Armored Infantry Doctrine. These three have their ups and downs, but the question is, which one suits our nation the best in terms of economy and flexibility.

focuses.name: Light Infantry Dominance
focuses.description: The foot soldier is the easiest one to mold and adapt to any situation. With this key we shall turn the lock and open the door to efficiency, letting our soldiers be able to handle threats, both on land or in the air.

focuses.name: Mobile Infantry Machine
focuses.description: Through the flexibility of the foot soldier, combined with the mobility of motorized transports and recon type vehicles, we strive to create the ultimate strike force that is the core of our army.

focuses.name: Armored Infantry Ascendance
focuses.description: Modern tanks are expensive and very costly for the potential "reward" they give. Therefore we must adapt our infantry to replace and stand in for these money sinks and create a new way forward. The armored infantry doctrine will secure versatility of armored combat, with the more efficient and flexible deployment of foot soldiers to take attention away and confuse both enemy armored and light force elements.

focuses.name: Tank Force Dilemma
focuses.description: The modern battlefield has nearly made the original use of the tank, obsolete. We must seriously consider what we intend to make use of these massive metal machines if we are to genuinely have a well rounded army.

focuses.name: Repurposing Armored Programs
focuses.description: The RAP directive is an immediate reorganization of the army. Tank forces will be nearly stopped and reserved for very specific duties if need be, however the main directive will be that the research and materials will be redirected towards IFV, APC and other programs to bolster and improve all other aspect of combat.

focuses.name: Modern Tanks, Means Modern Solutions
focuses.description: The tank is a modern marvel and should not be simply discarded as a gimmick of a bygone era. By refining production methods and retooling unit organizations we can make our tank force the big brother and traveling companion to our main infantry force.

focuses.name: Logistical Dominance
focuses.description: The army functions only when it actually has the equipment essential to maintain a combat effective force. We must therefore set an example by encouraging and expanding the logistical apparatus to ensure the timely and efficient conduct of our supply and logistical network.

focuses.name: Fire Support Supremacy
focuses.description: Artillery, the king of the battlefield. Mobility is versatile to one's designing needs, area clearing is effective in multiple ways and as an added bonus, can be relatively cheaper than calling in for a plane. As such we will invest and ensure our artillery is marked to be the new age bread winner of war, just like it was decades and even centuries before.

focuses.name: Gold Star Program
focuses.description: The modern battlefield is defined by the technological edge of our enemies. Though the arms race that was the Cold War is over, our enemies continue to grow day by day, as the "Era of Peace" continues to bubble and churn its way into a boiling hot stew of discontent, revolutions and social unrest. We must invest heavily in R&D programs, refine our technological integrations and ensure that we are not only army strong, but an army of one.

focuses.name: Armored Combat Debate
focuses.description: The modern queen of the battlefield is that of the armored fighting vehicle. Be it tanks, IFVs or APCs, these war machines can define a single battle and potentially even an entire campaign. However, as innovations in armored combat are made we have come into a split in the road. Do we focus more on tank based developments or do we reserve more for the lighter infantry support vehicles like IFVs and APCs.

focuses.name: Light Vehicle Innovations
focuses.description: While tanks are good at being mobile bunkers, the investments and innovations in modern AT capabilities makes direct tank combat a more risky investment in both material and personnel. Therefore we can redirect funding more towards APCs and IFVs to ensure a flexible infantry and armored approach. Besides APCs and IFVs are a lot easier to make modular then tanks are.

focuses.name: Modern Battle Tank Innovations
focuses.description: The MBT or Modern Battle Tank is a Cold War innovation that has created the modern standard of tank doctrine. We must utilize this and ensure we create a powerful armored force to punch and steel ourselves against any enemy attacks. As a byproduct of such innovations, units like SPAA and SPGs are likely to see passive innovations as we retool unit organizations to encompass more equal footing sub units.

focuses.name: Mass Motorization Efforts
focuses.description: To ensure our mobility to any metric we've chosen, we must compel our manufacturing partners to standardize and increase motorization production as to allow for our infantry to keep pace with our mechanized and armored elements.

focuses.name: The Artillery Conundrum
focuses.description: In a modern age of drones, aircraft with stealth and so much more distance bearing equipment, it's a matter of principle of what role we shall take with one of the arguably most vulnerable field units there is for the army. This being the artillery and its crew. We need to figure out just what direction we need to take it and if we are to focus more on defense or potential offense to prevent the enemy from just casually striking on these glaring targets.

focuses.name: Defensive Artillery Program
focuses.description: The DAP initiative is a program designed to research and innovate towards better defensive measures in both design of equipment as well as its ability to be defended in the field as a whole. Localized maneuverability and the ability to reach the frontlines from increased distances will also ensure the overall survivability of our equipment and crews.

focuses.name: Offensive Artillery Program
focuses.description: The OAP is to set a new standard of maneuver warfare for the entire force. Through innovations and research related to armor and Self Propelled Artillery systems, we set the pace of our entire army as the artillery is considered the slowest unit within the branch.

focuses.name: Supplies, Supplies, Supplies
focuses.description: The quartermaster corps is gearing up to be the backbone of the army's functionality. More advancements and complex weapons systems means more things to lug around and worry about replacing when in the field. We must therefore establish a fluid and maneuverable supply network to ensure the limitations of enemy destruction of "critical" supply hubs.

focuses.name: Army Special Forces Question
focuses.description: The Special Forces of the army service branch are becoming more numerous in both denominations and overlapping abilities. We need to seriously consider what role we want our army's special forces to have we are to not only be more distinctive from other branches, but also distinctive enough within our own branch of service.

focuses.name: Specialized Frontline Defense Support
focuses.description: The SFDP is a new reorganization of army special forces units into a general force or sub-branch of the army to aid and assist in defense positions in any and all ways possible. Potential encirclements means the SFDP would run limited supplies to help stranded troops, do counter fire and maneuver on enemy attacks on positions and or enemy recon units and so forth. With this, the army will be able to unify itself in a bulwark against the enemies of liberty and democracy itself.

focuses.name: The Dagger Within The Cloak
focuses.description: Our Special Forces Groups or SFGs, need to be the best of the best. As such to secure this lofty goal we will need substantial monetary and equipment investments to train, refine and grow this force into a strike force of the utmost effectiveness.

focuses.name: The Information Game
focuses.description: Knowing what you as well as what the enemy is doing is a key instrument in creating the muse of victory. We must invest in better ways to recon and acquire information from the enemy forces if we are to avoid wasteful losses.

focuses.name: This Is The Army Mr. Jones
focuses.description: We are an army new, new spirit, new soldiers and a new beginning to defending what is right. For freedom, liberty and the pursuit of happiness for all.

focuses.name: The United States Navy
focuses.description: Founded in 1776, disbanded after the revolution and then refounded as an emergency reaction to the Barbary Pirates of the time in the 1800s, the United States Navy has had a stoic and ever changing history. Being the forefront of innovations navally since over taking the British Empire around the time of the world wars, the US navy seeks to figure out just what it needs in the new millennia. With most combat being land or air centric, many in the public wonder just how much money does the navy needs. As such naval leadership needs to pivot its thinking and PR teams to justify any new decisions, for if the navy is to be more than a simple merchant defense fleet, then it must find its new voice in this new age.

focuses.name: Project Steel Waves
focuses.description: We are the superpower of the globe, not a badge of honor, not a demerit of shame, simply a status of order and position. To this avail we must adapt our naval reach to fit this status. Most global powers combined can't fully compete with our tech from nearly 40+ years ago and as such we will keep the R&D focused around streamlining production, repairs and modifications of existing ships. A modular and adaptive fleet of many, rather than a slowly shrinking fleet of raw tech and power.

focuses.name: Naval Group Flexibility Program
focuses.description: The NGFP is a designated productions program which will allow us to streamline and better adapt our naval production and repair efforts for maximum effectiveness.

focuses.name: Small Ship Debate
focuses.description: The modern age has recreated the small ship dynamic of frigates and corvettes as the cream of the crop. Well if we are to create a peak streamlined force we need to figure out which of these two will be the core which supports our subs and destroyers.

focuses.name: Frigate Fighters
focuses.description: Frigates, the most versatile and ever changing class of ship throughout naval history itself. This ship, while smaller than a destroyer can have the firepower of a cruiser if modified correctly. As such we'll turn our frigates into real fighters and the prime backbone of our navy.

focuses.name: Corvette Combat Flexibility
focuses.description: The corvette is the smallest reasonably combat effective vessel in a modern fleet's line up. As such we will invest, adapt, upgrade and create a corvette fleet which will overwhelm and destroy the enemies of liberty and free seas to travel.

focuses.name: Naval Maneuver Warfare
focuses.description: Investments into propulsion R&D efforts will allow our small vessels to be ever more nimble on the high seas. This ever increasing maneuverability is something most naval captains are not equipped or trained for and as such will need training and time to get use to these new ways of fighting.

focuses.name: Increasing Contractor Incentives
focuses.description: By creating better guidelines, incentive packages and funding, our naval civilian and military contractors will be better motivated to provide better results overall then previously earned.

focuses.name: Project New Waves
focuses.description: Project New Waves is a dedicated R&D initiative to renew, embolden and modernize as well as even future proof where ever and whenever possible. Our navy is the largest in the world by tonnage, so lets make ever last ton count.

focuses.name: The Submarine Debate
focuses.description: Submarines are the future to naval stealth and defensive measures. However we need to seriously figure out whether we will invest into our attack or missile variants of our submarine fleet.

focuses.name: The Attack Fleet
focuses.description: Through investments into our attack submarines, both pre-existing and future development of, we can assure our naval prowess is at its heartiest in targeting and swiftly destroying enemy vessels.

focuses.name: The Missile Fleet
focuses.description: Through extensive investments into modular missiles into our submarines, we'll be able to target and destroy any obstacle in the sea. Be they man made or nature if needed.

focuses.name: Aircraft Carrier Direction Dilemma
focuses.description: The role of the modern aircraft carrier is diverging. On one hand there is the traditional, "mobile airport" method. On the other hand there is the idea of a mobile gun and or missile platform which also leans into the helicopters over fixed winged aircraft. Whichever it is we need to figure it out and begin working on it like it was yesterday.

focuses.name: Mobile Airports Program
focuses.description: Through R&D in making more nimble aircraft as well as both launch and landing assist systems, we can look to make our carriers into mobile airports. This in turn will bring the most amount of firepower to a naval combat zone without extensive investments in core ships like destroyers, cruisers and so forth.

focuses.name: Project Attack Helicopter
focuses.description: Significant investments and research into developing better helicopters will allow them to be the new universal fighting machine. Though by proxy improving helicopters helps with land combat, the primary purpose is to use them to be nimble and fast strikers in our carrier fleets. The modern naval strike force is here and we're here to make it happen.

focuses.name: Strengthening Naval Training Efforts
focuses.description: Through increased standards and requirements as well as overall improvements to how and what we train into our naval personnel. As such we will set a new precedent on how the average sailor responds to battlefield conditions and crisis management situations to create a stronger and more knowledgeable force.

focuses.name: Role Of The USMC
focuses.description: The United States Marine Corps has had a bloodied history. However the role of the marine corps is being challenged once more. In the modern age of isolated campaigns and no "grand war" with a foe that can be easily identified, the identity of the modern marine is a bit different. We need to figure out if we should continue to have a specialized Marine Corps or institute a more support and or generalization of the branch and move it towards the army, rather than a sub-department strictly under the navy.

focuses.name: Marines Are As Marines Were
focuses.description: Launching naval invasions and the spear to pierce an enemy coastal defense. That is the Marine Corps and that is what she will be. Marines Lead The Way!

focuses.name: Marine Lessons In Army Clothes
focuses.description: The modern battlefield has lesser and lesser needs for a strong and dedicated naval invasion force. As such we can work to integrate and better reform our ground forces to be more adaptable to terrain features, be they water or non-water based.

focuses.name: Repair Teams
focuses.description: Outfitting specialized teams of Marines to help repairs and damage control means our ships can get back out on the water faster than ever before. Leaving only severe issues for the dry docks if and when need be.

focuses.name: A Modern Navy
focuses.description: Through thick and thin we've done it, we've made a navy to rival even our strongest foes. Now we shall be able to defend both ourselves and our allies without fail.

focuses.name: United States Air Force
focuses.description: Despite being one of the youngest armed forces branches, the USAF has an interesting history. Originally a department of the army under the name USAAF or United States Army Air Force, the demands of world war 2 would require the air force to become its own service branch. Since that war the air force has become the poster child for the modern age in battlefield supremacy. But as warfare changes so does the needs of the air force, now as a new age dawns on the branch leadership needs to figure out just how to adapt to the ever changing situation of what is the, "modern battlefield".

focuses.name: Economy Class Warfare
focuses.description: You can't fight a war on an empty stomach and you sure as shit can't fight it without a functioning economy. We must therefore find ways to retool our air force budgeting to be efficient in production methods and models that in turn we could put back into the economy itself.

focuses.name: The Modular Design Program
focuses.description: The MDP is a streamlining of all aircraft production. Instead of creating multiple hyper specific aircraft production lines, we can ensure the most efficient production by creating a real standard aircraft model which can be modularly adapted to the needs of the nation.

focuses.name: Production Development Investments
focuses.description: Through R&D initiatives and general manufacturing investments, we can grow our production capabilities as well as churn over some civilian results as well. These will certainly help create jobs and fine tune our aircraft's capabilities.

focuses.name: Aeronautical Development Board
focuses.description: The ADB is a dedicated institute for developing aviation based advancements, be they safety, weapons systems or whatever the case may be. However to not stretch our funding to thin and to not overly burden the population, we need to decide just what direction these advancements may go. We can either look towards securing air supremacy or we could look into more ground support and or bombing capabilities as a whole. Either choice will determine what we need to worry about in the future should war arise.

focuses.name: Fighter Focused Budgeting
focuses.description: Lighter materials, agility training improvements and better weapons systems. These are just some of what we intend to invest in to allow our air force to be certainly a force to be reckoned with.

focuses.name: Bomber Focused Budgeting
focuses.description: Increased payload damage abilities, improved aircraft system designs and so forth. These and more will be invested in to ensure our air force will flatten any and all obstacles that our ground forces encounter.

focuses.name: Civil & Military Innovations Program
focuses.description: A joint development and research facility, the C&MIP is designed to combine military innovations and civilian ones and understand how one can inspire the other and vise versa. With this our economy will be built for the people as well as for their defense.

focuses.name: A Limitless Sky
focuses.description: They say the sky is the limit, well the United States Air Force will make it the very goal of the branch to exceed and prove that there is no such limit.

focuses.name: Perpetual Air Dominance
focuses.description: Through near constant investments in weapon systems and crew training regimens, we can create a state of perpetual dominance through sheer aggression.

focuses.name: American Institute For Avionics
focuses.description: The AIA is a research center focused on developing and bettering our air force's capabilities. We hope in the future to create great things to come.

focuses.name: Phase One Innovations
focuses.description: Phase 1 innovations refers to general advancements in crew training as well as more efficient ways in handling and or making aircraft.

focuses.name: Phase Two Innovations
focuses.description: Continued investments and research initiatives have begun to see results in relation to ground support and direct battlefield support. We hope these innovations will better improve our combined assaults on enemy positions.

focuses.name: Phase Three Innovations
focuses.description: Aggressive investments continue to soar our innovations as we have breakthroughs in large bomber aircraft and payload destructive power.

focuses.name: The Paratrooper Corps
focuses.description: The paratroopers has been a unique branch of the army and air force. Born out of experimental need from the demands of world war two, the paratroopers are considered a key part of modern training. From traditional jumps from C-130s to rappelling out of attack helicopters, the paratrooper spirit is still strong in today's battlefield. Now we need to figure out the real needs of our military forces to ensure peak cohesion and effectiveness.

focuses.name: Jump Wings Forever
focuses.description: Our paratroopers are the best of the best, we will improve and tend to this force to ensure they stay that way for the foreseeable future.

focuses.name: Every Soldier A Trooper
focuses.description: The mobility of helicopters as well as the ever rapid changing pace of the battlefields means that the role of a paratrooper needs to be expanded upon and not just reserved. As such we will do whatever we can to refine and enhance our army with the lessons learned by the paratroopers over the years.

focuses.name: Joint Branch Coordination Training
focuses.description: The JBCT program is a cohesion and coordination training program to increase training and cooperation efforts between the air force and army branches of service due to the innate nature of the modern battlefield. This will also help to decrease blue on blue incidents between the branches where possible.

focuses.name: To Infinity And Beyond!
focuses.description: Our innovations and dedication to ensure our air force is unmatched by anyone have been great. We can say without a doubt that our efforts to better our air force will be the talk of the world for years to come.

focuses.name: Joint Chiefs of Staff For The United States
focuses.description: The JCS as well as the General Officer Corps of the United States is a temperamental one at best and a soft power struggle at worse depending on the era. However the GOC in the recent years has seen some interesting issues. Internal struggles on corruption and over zealous spending despite the end of the cold war as well as a just the age old question of, "innovators vs old guards". In the new millennia however the question of retraining and refining the officer corps as a whole is up for debate and as such ideas are being thrown around. As such we need to figure out what our needs will be.

focuses.name: Army Centric Training
focuses.description: By furthering retraining and advancement programs around the army, our priority in command & control developments will see our ground forces excel in the coming times.

focuses.name: Army Knowledge Priority
focuses.description: Advancement within the officer corps ranks will now require more army based knowledge and needs than of the air force or navy. This will ensure more C&C elements go towards improving our ground forces where the bulk of fighting happens.

focuses.name: Naval Centric Training
focuses.description: By furthering retraining and advancement programs around the navy, our priority in command & control will go to benefiting naval maneuvering and survivability. Meaning more ships will have flexible and adaptable commanders.

focuses.name: Naval Knowledge Priority
focuses.description: Advancements within the officer corps will now need more naval based knowledge to grow and develop better C&C elements within our naval branch. Most of our strategic fighting involves the navy in some way or another, as such to make sure this backbone is strong and durable, its leaders need to be made of a similar stock.

focuses.name: Air Force Centric Training
focuses.description: By furthering retraining and advancement programs around the air force, our priority in command & control developments will see our air forces excel in the coming times.

focuses.name: Air Force Priority Knowledge
focuses.description: Advancements within the officer corps will now need more air and or aviation based knowledge to grow and develop better C&C elements within our air force. The modern battlefield is nearly defined by the air war, as such we need to ensure our air force is un-challengeable by any known foe.

focuses.name: A True Pax Americana
focuses.description: Reforms, changes, tending to the needs of every last branch of service under our authority. Our nation will be secured and the world will know what a True American peace shall be. Ad pacem et felicitatem. "To Peace and Prosperity".

focuses.name: Re-introducing Mandatory Service
focuses.description: Through congressional lobbying we can hopefully push through the re-introduction of a mandatory service period. This can keep our numbers up and put less strain on the purely volunteer force we have. Since the backlash politically will be a lot, the period recommended to law makers is only 6 months.

focuses.name: Expanding Mandatory Service
focuses.description: The needs of the armed forces and national defense have grown to a point of concern. If we are to keep on top of things we must and I mean we must lobby congress to approve of such a measure. The public backlash will be sizeable but in the end of it, our national defense in these ever trying times of uncertainty are a justification.

focuses.name: Concerning Development
focuses.description: Things are not going well and it's reaching a point that is not seeming reversible. As such we must increase the conscription requirements to force in the numbers we need. It'll hurt, but we can't risk any debate.

focuses.name: Desperate Measures
focuses.description: Things continue to grow worse, drastic action is needed if we are to get anywhere. Equipment means nothing if we don't have the men and women to use it.

focuses.name: US Plan On Foreign Policy
focuses.description: The ongoing civil wars in West Africa will prove a good staging ground to mold out foreign policy, but we are not sure if it will define it.

focuses.name: Support the Democratic Movement
focuses.description: They look to want freedom and a strong nation, we must support them.

focuses.name: Support the Nationalist Movement
focuses.description: They look to want freedom and a strong nation, we must support them.

focuses.name: The Salesman Approach
focuses.description: The people don't want a war, but they also don't want to sit idly. To do that we can stand to gain for our people and the world if we start promoting training and equipment deals to those in need.

focuses.name: Supplying Our Sierra Leone
focuses.description: The people of Sierra Leone are under equipped and we must help them.

focuses.name: Meeting with African Union Members
focuses.description: The continent of Africa is vast and unpredictable at best, to remedy this we must meet leaders of the African Union in order to better understand the complexity and clientele we could have.

focuses.name: Securing Trade with Africa
focuses.description: The continent is rich with resources and as such promoting mutual trades will better our nation and our influence on the continent.

focuses.name: The Humanitarian Approach
focuses.description: The people don't want a war, but they also don't want to sit idly. We must send a message and the best way to do that is via humanitarianism.

focuses.name: Advising Sierra Leone
focuses.description: The nation is decently equipped but haphazardly trained, we must help get them more training if we are to hope for their victory.

focuses.name: Meeting EU Leadership
focuses.description: The Europeans held the continent of Africa for millennia to where they must have the most info about how to handle the continent. We can get a better understanding of the trouble we may have if we talk with them.

focuses.name: Coordinated Help
focuses.description: The French have a foreign legion and so should we, we must change our image and solidify our claim to world peace and freedom.

focuses.name: The Interventionist Will
focuses.description: The people want a war but we can't sit idly by. We must send a message and strike fear into the enemies of our nation and show them we are still standing strong.

focuses.name: Sierra Leone "Peacekeepers"
focuses.description: The nation is decently equipped but isn't making any real progress, we can send "peacekeepers" as if we were attached to the UN and help motivate the war in a more positive direction.

focuses.name: State Visit to the United Kingdom
focuses.description: The United Kingdom used to be the colonial overseer in the Sierra Leone territory and must have the best knowledge to help us in this little endeavor, it may also help us in any other conflicts in the former British Empire's territory.

focuses.name: Joint "Police Action"
focuses.description: The Police Action which has been the Sierra Leone Civil War is looking promising towards a new kind of foreign policy. We must look to refine and redefine the term "Police Action" lest many start repeating Vietnam war time sentiments.

focuses.name: State Visit To Canada
focuses.description: To the north we look for friendship and security, lest we alienate those in our front yard.

focuses.name: State Visit To Mexico
focuses.description: To the south we look for peace and stability, for we should not forget our backyard as well.

focuses.name: State Visit To Brazil
focuses.description: Our neighbors to the south, we mustn't forget them, for where would our hemispheric hegemony be without our biggest southern continental counterpart. We shall check in and help where we can.

focuses.name: The Afghanistan Question
focuses.description: With the recent attacks on the nation the terrorist sparked Civil War in Afghanistan has been in our military's thoughts for a while and we have reason to believe that the leader of the attacks is running this cabal. So we must think of how we are going to respond.

focuses.name: Arming Our Horse
focuses.description: The troubling situation in Afghanistan is of vital international importance so that we can do what we can to support the more stable of the factions.

focuses.name: Muslim Legion
focuses.description: A portion of our muslim population wishes to go and fight to defend what was once their homeland, since the conflict looks to be stagnant at best this may be a great opportunity.

focuses.name: Arming the Legion
focuses.description: The legion is not too well equipped, as such we must at least show courtesy and supply them.

focuses.name: Advising the Legion
focuses.description: The Northern Alliance is not very… proficient to say the least, but with a little education and we'll whip into enough shape. With these more laid back but pointed paths many are beginning to understand the sort of Passive Aggressive strategy the foreign office is trying out.

focuses.name: Indirect Support of Freedom
focuses.description: The stability of the Middle East is under threat, we've tested ourselves in Sierra Leone but now we face a real challenge.

focuses.name: Supplying Democracy
focuses.description: The Northern Alliance is in a bad state compared to the Fundamentalist faction it faces and as such we must help them out in core supplies.

focuses.name: Modern War Advisors
focuses.description: The Northern Alliance knows the tactics of its enemy, but they lack discipline and will. We must reform their training programs if they are to ever be a real fighting force.

focuses.name: Anti-Terror Training
focuses.description: Our modern enemies require modern training programs. We must reform and institute anti-terror based training programs as a way to help our forces adapt.

focuses.name: Starting the War on Terror
focuses.description: The war on terror has begun and the first international threat has come from central Asia. Afghanistan is home to those who harmed our nation and we will strike back with a vengeance.

focuses.name: Establishing a Force
focuses.description: The Northern Alliance as it's been called is a bunch of rag tags, if we are to secure the region we are going to have to send some forces there to shore up what they can't hold.

focuses.name: Changing the Rules
focuses.description: These terrorists have caused so much of a headache in such a short time period. To many it looks as if we just re-entered Vietnam, but unfortunately it's way worse. Our forces are being attritioned out to a point where the locals are on a pendulum of opinion towards us.

focuses.name: Adaptive Tactics
focuses.description: Our troops need to adapt and as such we need to invest in changing our doctrine of war if we are to make any real headway.

focuses.name: State Visit Iran
focuses.description: Our biggest regional contender to contemplate is that of the State of Iran, a precarious sort, they nevertheless can cause trouble if we upset them too much.

focuses.name: State Visit Russia
focuses.description: Our biggest rival is of course the successor state of the now defunct Soviet Union, we must distract the Russian Federation if we are to solidify our interest in the region.

focuses.name: State Visit India
focuses.description: India is a growing power, if we invest in forging a relation of friend and or partnership then we are sure to secure our interest along with having a formidable power within the greater Middle East/Central Asian area.

focuses.name: Iraq Leadership Problems
focuses.description: The recent encroachment of the leader of the state of Iraq has caused us great concern with so much investments into the nation of Kuwait, we must look to find a solution if we are to solidify our interest in the Middle East.

focuses.name: Oil for Aid
focuses.description: The leader of Iraq is a man of charisma and vigor, but we must find a way to curb his more selfish side if we are to avoid anything prolonging.

focuses.name: Integrated Defenses
focuses.description: The Negotiations have come through and it's looking like there may be a fight. Depending on the details we could be involved in a passive or a more aggressive manner, the people will surely be upset at such a prospect.

focuses.name: Every Man a TOW
focuses.description: The dawn of a new conflict is upon us, though we stand to gain significantly from this and as such we must make the best short term gains if we are to understand the long term goal and price for which we can earn from the coming endeavor.

focuses.name: Political Oligarchs
focuses.description: The current troubles in the Middle East have started to simmer down, regardless of the outcome. The best thing is that we secured what we wanted and that our people will be satiated with the cheaper goods which shall come from these most recent gains.

focuses.name: Kuwait Defensive Aid
focuses.description: The oil in Kuwait is vast and the leadership of Iraq knows this, so we have a lot of invested interest in the resources and stability of the region and as such we must preserve the Kuwait peoples and their nation.

focuses.name: Limited Supplies
focuses.description: The Kuwait nations' economy is mostly oil, we can preserve this but at a cost. We'll send them a simple but direct array of armaments and transports to support their forces.

focuses.name: Increased Advisors
focuses.description: The Kuwait army is not the best but is still comparable in training towards the Iraqi army. To remedy this we must send modern advisors to help train and harden the resolve and combat ability of the Kuwait army.

focuses.name: Arab Legion
focuses.description: The Arab peoples of our nation wish to defend their old home, their region's stability and to send a message to those who abuse their peoples. Therefore an Arab Legion will be established, this will of course take from those wanting to fight in our forces but it will surely bolster the Kuwait Army strength.

focuses.name: War on Terror - Phase Two
focuses.description: The growing threat of Iraq's leader is cause for great concern for the stability of the Middle East, to this knowledge we must act despite the potential backlash we may suffer.

focuses.name: Protecting our Assets
focuses.description: The oil fields of Kuwait are of vital importance and as such we will defend them to the best resolve if provoked.

focuses.name: Increased Deployment
focuses.description: There are rumors and intel about some very hostile acts being committed against the Iraqi peoples and against the national sovereignty of Kuwait, we must begin preparations if we are to be ready. Our people are sure to be a bit disgruntled but the feeling will pass.

focuses.name: The WMD Cause
focuses.description: Our intelligence services report the possibility of WMDs being present inside the nation of Iraq and this is something for which neither we nor the free world can stand, as such Operation Desert Storm is to commence and we will deal with Saddam personally and free the peoples of Iraq.

focuses.name: State Visit to Turkey
focuses.description: The nation of Turkey is a nice buffer between Russia and the Middle East. We must improve our standing to ensure our interests are assured.

focuses.name: State Visit to Egypt
focuses.description: Egypt is one of the strongest nations in the region and we could use that strength to help protect the trade of the Suez and the resources we need.

focuses.name: State Visit to Saudi Arabia
focuses.description: Saudi Arabia is the richest nation in oil and one of the largest nations in the Arabian Peninsula, therefore we must secure a friendship for economic and strategic reasons.

focuses.name: The Arab Spring
focuses.description: The Syrian regime has been doing some questionable acts and unfortunately it looks to have boiled over. The Arab Spring seems to have dawned on the Syrian nation and the resulting protests have bubbled over into an all out civil war.

focuses.name: Monetary Policy
focuses.description: The MidEast is not a huge concern since our domestic supply and investment in other areas supplements us, however that does not mean we should just sit idly by. Let's give our defense contractors something to do shall we.

focuses.name: Arms to the Highest Bidder
focuses.description: The war for Syria rages and practically stalemates, as such let's liven things up by making some back channel offers.

focuses.name: Foreign Aid
focuses.description: The international community is weary of our more or less candid silence towards the mideast crisis. Let's try and calm this view by giving some "foreign aid" to those fighting for the "right" cause.

focuses.name: Everyone Has Their Price
focuses.description: The war has been dragging on for some time now and the last thing we need is to leave empty handed. We can pressure one or multiple groups into a compromise or some "mutual" benefit for us if they say their faction wins the war.

focuses.name: Advisory Policy
focuses.description: The Syrian Civil War is an international crisis which is affecting the stability of the whole mideast region, if we don't help out it will surely affect us and our allies.

focuses.name: Sending Advisors
focuses.description: The international community won't know anything if we send advisors, but these advisors need equipment to train with so lets give them some.

focuses.name: Backdoor Arms Dealing
focuses.description: The training is slow and equipment losses are mounting, let's organize a deal outside of the public eye to ensure the idea of equipment preservation in the Syrian forces.

focuses.name: Forming the Damascus Legion
focuses.description: The Foreign Legion of the US is expanding, volunteers which are arab or former Syrians are willing to go fight for their home. We can't deny them this right lest the nation were to fall to more unsavory types.

focuses.name: The Syrian Terror
focuses.description: The terrorist which make up the Authoritarian Syrian government and those terror cells developing because of the war must be solved to protect our assets and the global economy, we must act now or risk seeing another oil crisis.

focuses.name: Sending Volunteer Forces
focuses.description: The international community is organizing a joint force to help the democratic rebels in Syria and as such we must muster our own force to stand out and lead the way.

focuses.name: Keeping Supplies Steady
focuses.description: The war will be quick, but it will only be as quick as our logistics hold up. We must do something to steady the supply stream lest we face combat issues and morale issues for the troops on the ground.

focuses.name: Indiscriminate Bombings
focuses.description: The terrorists are blurring the lines of warfare to a point where Vietnam is looking like a checkers game. If we are too cautious then we risk letting vital targets get away, but if we are too aggressive we risk the civilian and international community turning against us...war truly is hell.

focuses.name: State Visit to Russia
focuses.description: The betterment of our relations with the old foe is to the benefit of all. We must look to be more cordial towards the Russian people and its government.

focuses.name: 2nd State Visit to Saudi Arabia
focuses.description: The Saudi nation is a good regional power within the Middle East and as such we must build relations in order to secure our interests in the region.

focuses.name: State Visit to the Arab Union
focuses.description: The Arab Union is a collection of states which safe guard a lot of strategic regions in Africa and the Middle East. As such improving relations with its leaders should help make future negotiations smoother or in hope, easier for our benefit.

focuses.name: The Regulatory Merry-Go-Round
focuses.description: Congressional regulators seem to always want to play games with what needs and doesn't need to be regulated. As such many see this as spinning a wheel and hoping for the best outcome.

focuses.name: Pacific States Regional Assessment
focuses.description: The Pacific States has a very tight balance. From good resources to terrible water allocation congress must decide what is a priority for the people and the future for the region and the wider United States.

focuses.name: Targeted Growth Programs
focuses.description: By targeting under developed areas of the Pacific States, the money allocated will hopefully pay itself off with taxes.

focuses.name: Mini Minerals Act
focuses.description: Congress has passed the Mini Minerals Act, a limited plan to develop a domestic rubber supply to help regional economics and national supplies.

focuses.name: The Conservation Act
focuses.description: With the passing of the Conservation Act, localities within the Pacific States will be able to clear and conserve what is needed to help the people and the respective economies.

focuses.name: Rare Elements Initiative
focuses.description: Targeting Mining regulations and overruling state regulations we can start a domestic supply of rare metals and materials needed for domestic consumption. This should boost the local economy and help our nation in the long run.

focuses.name: Loosening Pacific Zoning Laws
focuses.description: Softening the cumbersome and almost counterproductive zoning laws have stalled proper development. By loosening these we can spur local development and generate more tax revenue.

focuses.name: The Reservoir Act
focuses.description: The Reservoir Act will enable the creation of new reservoirs as a way to grow local economies and increase water availability for low and minimal water access areas.

focuses.name: The Near Western States
focuses.description: From the Great Plains and the Pacific States comes the gap which is the Near Western States. Famous for the Rocky mountains this region is one of the least developed and the most challenging of the regions. Congress must proceed with caution when trekking the deserts, mountains and vast geography that is the Near Western States.

focuses.name: The Salt Lake Regulatory Commission
focuses.description: The Salt Lake Commission on Regulations will observe and approach the current mining operations and look to expand while minimizing environmental impacts.

focuses.name: The Rocky Preservation Act
focuses.description: The Rocky Mountains are a national landmark and many would hate to see such a symbol of America be destroyed. As such the established committee has found ways to turn tourism into a preservation movement. This'll please local economies and the environmentalist as well.

focuses.name: Phoenix Arms Contract
focuses.description: Military contractors have sought out areas around Phoenix and Arizona as a whole and are looking to establish some manufacturing facilities. We must work to help boost our military and the local economy with jobs.

focuses.name: Rocky Mount-Go-A
focuses.description: Like the Rocky movies we must learn and train our way to better understanding our opponent. Unlike the movie however our adversary is a geological formation. Loosening regulations around mining operations for the mountain range we can look to extract new and more resources for domestic supply and production means.

focuses.name: Breaching The Western Gap
focuses.description: The Deserts and Mountains which inhibit the smooth traveling of our citizenry is what messes with supply chains and local commerce. We must find ways to create arteries and bring jobs, people and free-er movement to the Near Western States.

focuses.name: More Than Just Potatoes
focuses.description: Idaho is a lush farmland known for its potatoes, however agriculture shouldn't be the only thing the state is known for. By investing and expanding local industries we can make Idaho the icon for the Near West.

focuses.name: The Greater Plains Region
focuses.description: The Greater Plains which encompasses a lot of territory is considered the bread basket of the nation. While we are glad to be able to have a good food supply our diversity in economic terms in the region is very lacking. To this congress must look to implement plans which it sees fit to better develop and help the region catch up to the rest of the union.

focuses.name: Dakotan Risk Assessment Committee
focuses.description: The Committee is to be established as a joint interstate based company which will see the development of rubber based products using the oil supplies from North Dakota to create new jobs and of course new rubber supplies.

focuses.name: Great Plains And Great Cities
focuses.description: The urban centers of these sparse states are very under developed and as such targeted programs shall be instituted to help the domino effect of city sprawling to help further develop these states.

focuses.name: Kansas City Arms Manufacturer
focuses.description: A new contract has been leased out and the partners agree that these new plants should be established in Kansas City. Its urban but also isolated nature makes the plants less likely to be messed with.

focuses.name: The Nebraska Act
focuses.description: Following up on our bread basket region of the country we have the center belt which is North Dakota to Kansas. Using Nebraska as a staging ground we will draw more jobs and people to better develop this overly specialized region of the country.

focuses.name: The Minraculture Act
focuses.description: The mining and agriculture of the great plains region is very diverse but also untapped. Using geological surveys and risk assessment we shall be able to start up new mining operations and grow our domestic supply of needed mineral resources.

focuses.name: The Hydroponics Act
focuses.description: While hydroponics is still a more infantile method, there is no reason why we couldn't propel this to greater understanding. As such initiatives will be set up to create designated areas for the development and testing of these large scale experiments.

focuses.name: The Lone South
focuses.description: The Lone South comprises of Texas, Arkansas, Louisiana, Oklahoma and New Mexico. These states are a vast mix of very and very not developed, as such congress must look to balance these states and their lacking parts to allow the region to prosper and join the nation.

focuses.name: The Red River Commission
focuses.description: The Red River Commission is a mutual body comprised of members from Texas and Oklahoma as a way to bind the two in looking for effective resource expansions. Using Texas Oil to create new petrochemical related jobs and resources along with a notable iron ore deposit in Oklahoma has seen the eyes of both parties to come to an understanding.

focuses.name: The CenSouth Zoning Reforms Act
focuses.description: The vast plains and mixtures of terrain have made for confusing zoning, as such this zoning reforms act will be used to streamline and make efficient the construction zones needed for developing these lacking regions within the states.

focuses.name: The Rio Grande Shipyard
focuses.description: The Texas Shipyards are moderate for what they need, however with the rising interest in national security, foreign demands and domestic demands alike, many have petitioned for more or expansions to this existing job market. With this in mind congress along with the state of Texas' legislature have created a joint company known as the Rio Grande Shipworks to meet this need.

focuses.name: The Austin Investment Firm
focuses.description: The Austin Investment Firm is a government initiative to create jobs in the more rural areas of the Lone South States which is using Texas as a central hub to create its investments.

focuses.name: Unregulated Destiny To Manifest
focuses.description: While many see manifest destiny as a foregone page of history, the modern citizen must look to manifest his own destiny. We can't allow the limiting laws of land acquisition prevent this, as such deregulation in these matters is what they shall get.

focuses.name: The Lone Mining Company
focuses.description: With the modern manifest destiny mindset, congress and the states of New Mexico and Oklahoma have created the Lone Mining Company, which was sponsored by the Austin Investment Firm. With the changes in land acquisition laws and mining laws in the region, the company hopes to find and expand the domestic supply of needed raw materials to bolster domestic job creation.

focuses.name: The Greater Lakes Region
focuses.description: While the states along the great lakes are considered the Great Lake States, the surrounding ones of Minnesota, Iowa, Missouri and Kentucky are what some call the Greater Lake States due to blending cultures of their "associated" regions. These states comprise areas of heavy agriculture and what was a large industrial sector. Now it's up to congress to bring balance and reforms to this region of the country.

focuses.name: The Milwaukee Mining Firm
focuses.description: A regional mineral extraction firm has been set up in Milwaukee. Their goal is simple, set up or expand existing vital resource operations to bolster domestic job growth.

focuses.name: From Rust To Refined
focuses.description: The Rust Belt gets its name from the ever decreasing vitality of the manufacturing sector. Therefore we must invest to revitalize this to prevent further rusting of this industrial belt.

focuses.name: Lakeside Hubs
focuses.description: The Great Lakes make for attractive tourist sites, by prioritizing zoning in these hot spots we could look into better developing businesses and tourist ventures.

focuses.name: The Erie Boom Act
focuses.description: Lake Erie is a central hub for trade with Canada and a mixture of tourism and other businesses. The region has not been in good shape for a while, as such we must inject a direct investment to diversify and revitalize the economies of the localities around this great lake.

focuses.name: The Diversity Act
focuses.description: The Diversity Act will enable funds to be allocated to states who request the need of diversification in their economies. This can limit the overall monetary need and allow for a consensus on what the states are "to specialized" in to be not so dependent, economically speaking that is.

focuses.name: The Sprawling Act
focuses.description: Like the tendrils of a deep sea creature the regions' mining sector is extremely lacking, therefore emphasis on expanding and focusing on needed rarer mineral resources will be prioritized in these sponsored initiatives for local mining companies.

focuses.name: The Southeastern Region
focuses.description: The Southeast, also known as the "Deep South", is a region of extremes. Some areas are superbly developed while others look as if the settlers never saw it. While we want to preserve out nation's beauty congress must nevertheless look to balance these states of the Southern United States.

focuses.name: The Gulf Ports Act
focuses.description: The Gulf is a strategic hub and also a resource rich one. The shipping industry is heavy in these parts and as such the ports and shipyards must be expanded and overhauled for the overall betterment of the respective states.

focuses.name: The Urbanized Forests Act
focuses.description: The act which congress has passed will look to create developmental incentives to move and better spread the urbanized population of states like Mississippi. This way the respective states and their economies can diversify and expand at a larger and or faster rate as a wider foundation is created.

focuses.name: The Mobile Mineral Act
focuses.description: The Mobile Mineral Act is a bill which reforms and incentivize the development and limited strategical expansion of mining operations in states that are known for minerals not so easily mined. These initiatives will help make jobs and grow domestic supplies.

focuses.name: The Dixie Development Scheme
focuses.description: The DDS is a program designed to work from the inside out. By creating a strong base in what is considered the "heart of dixie", that being the states of Alabama and Mississippi, these states will help create a ripple effect of development of the wider southeastern region.

focuses.name: The Carolina Cultivation Program
focuses.description: The Carolinas are a mixed breed and as such we must help to develop the states agriculture base to further support an increase in industrial jobs. Remember, the food has to come from somewhere for the cities.

focuses.name: The Shining Act
focuses.description: The Shining Act is a host of mining reforms aimed at expanding domestic regional mining operations to better experiment with the ores available and the abilities to make said operations profitable in the long run.

focuses.name: The Capital Region
focuses.description: The states surrounding the capital area of D.C. are a fairly well-off region. Nevertheless this doesn't mean we shouldn't exclude them from economic investments and as such it will be up to congress on what those investments may be.

focuses.name: The Parkersburg Economic Committee
focuses.description: The PEC is a joint Interstate Commerce Committee to assess and grow targeted economic fall backs as a way to boost the local economics of the less developed regions of the states of the region.

focuses.name: The Atlantic Act
focuses.description: The Atlantic Act is a maritime development program to boost local communities and their related industries.

focuses.name: The Roanoke Mineral Act
focuses.description: This Mineral Act is a targeted growth act which will expand local jobs, domestic supplies of raw materials and overall should encourage a developmental ripple effect on the targeted states.

focuses.name: The Mary Lands Act
focuses.description: Congress has passed an interconnected economies act, wherein the developments of one state are to go hand in hand in helping the developments of another. The hope is encouraging domestic trade, consumption and a more "buy local" kind of mentality.

focuses.name: The Appalachian Reforms
focuses.description: The Appalachian Reforms is a series of mining reforms which should encourage local developments and expansions of existing mining operations in things like iron ore and energy resources.

focuses.name: The Delaware Act
focuses.description: The Delaware Act's main goal is as such: a mix of maritime and tourist industry growth programs to find ways to grow and interconnect their needs on one another.

focuses.name: The Northeastern Region
focuses.description: Famous for the northeast corridor the northeastern section of the US is an almost continual mass of urban sprawl. However the further inland you move in these states the more nature you find. Congress must look to create policies which balance where to develop so the preservation of the region's nature can stay as high as possible.

focuses.name: The Vershire Act
focuses.description: Using the basis of the tetris pieces for states, Vermont and New Hampshire will lead a targeted investment scheme which will help to expand further into other states in the region.

focuses.name: The Albany Development Program
focuses.description: The ADP is a program slated to help diversify the local economies starting from the greater Albany area and working eastward.

focuses.name: The Hartford Mining Act
focuses.description: With this act local mining companies and new mineral investments will be made, while the impact is not slated to be a large outcome, the projected mined resources are looking to be quite diverse.

focuses.name: The Kingston Reforms
focuses.description: These reforms center around redevelopment firms and loosening regulations in zoning, the hope being that open lots can be acquired faster and speed up the planning and subsequent construction processes.

focuses.name: The New Haven Mineral Reforms
focuses.description: This mineral legislation will see the development of mines in relation to more scarce resources in need. Though the northeast is not really a hotbed per se, this region nevertheless can provide more than what it already is.

focuses.name: The Newer England Act
focuses.description: With New reforms, new developments and a new page in the region's economic prosperity it is only right to establish a newer spin on the older areas. Therefore developments related to the core of the region will be implemented to fully revitalize and grow this nature and urban filled beauty that is the northeast.

focuses.name: Revitalize the Space Program
focuses.description: Nearly 60 years ago, NASA launched Apollo 11, successfully landing the first human on the Moon, winning the Space Race. Afterward, we Americans sank into complacency, as space lost its wonder. No more! It is time to renew our efforts and push back the final frontier.
